title: PseudoForge: a multi-engine pseudopotential generator and validator
description:
PseudoForge generates and validates pseudopotentials by driving nine independent atomic structure codes — Quantum ESPRESSO's ld1, ONCVPSP, the Vanderbilt ultrasoft generator, fhi98PP, OPIUM, the Goedecker-Teter-Hutter fitting toolchain, AtomPAW, the Atomic Pseudopotential Engine and ADPACK — through a single interface, in pure Bash with no Python dependency.

It reproduces published libraries from those libraries' own published parameters rather than approximating them: PSlibrary is reproduced byte-identically (apart from two caesium decks where upstream is physically impossible, as declared in ERRATA.tsv), and the GTH coefficient tables are reproduced exactly for all 322 published element-functional combinations. Where a library's parameters are not published, PseudoForge says so and labels its own construction as such rather than issuing it under the library's name.

Validation asks each engine for its own analysis rather than forcing one engine's test on all of them, and records which analysis produced each verdict. Every run writes a provenance file recording the engine version and a fingerprint of the binary that ran, because two builds of the same engine version do not produce the same pseudopotential.

The source archives for eight of the nine engines are bundled in the repository under engines-src/, so ./install.sh --bootstrap builds them offline; Quantum ESPRESSO (ld1) is fetched and built on demand the first time a run needs it.
